svg.title: mod-ui expanded: the way there and the way back
svg.desc: Every program around mod-ui with both directions of each link: the browser and the cloud, the modules of the Python process, the HMI, Control Chain, mod-host, JACK and MIDI devices, plus the events mod-host sends, the path of a MIDI message up to the browser, and who writes which files.
svg.metadata:
GENERATED by docs/mod-ui/diagrams/src/build.py from specs.py (architecture-expanded). Do not edit this file by hand. Content of the diagram as Mermaid or plain data (a summary for readers and AI tools; the layout lives in specs.py):

Files, the events on :5556 and the MIDI path are listed in the panels of the diagram.
svg.text: MOD-UI · ONE PYTHON PROCESS · ONE THREAD
value moved by MIDI or a CC pedal
LV2 parameter changed by a plugin
MIDI learn finished: becomes an addressing
loads a pedalboard or a snapshot
tempo or play changed (Link, MIDI clock)
end of a batch; waits for output_data_ready
JSON, used only by the page
HOW A MIDI MESSAGE REACHES THE UI
1 A USB or DIN port appears in JACK (system:midi_*, ttymidi:MIDI_in)
2 It reaches mod-host:midi_in, directly or through mod-midi-merger
3 mod-host applies it in the audio thread: mapped CC, program change,
beat clock, MIDI learn. The audio changes here, without mod-ui
4 mod-host queues an event and writes it on :5556
5 Host updates plugins[id] and calls msg_callback
6 Session writes the frame to every /websocket
7 host.js moves the widget (param_set, midi_map, transport)

g.text: $.ajax to mod-ui and to the cloud; relays downloads and uploads
answers ping and data_ready, turns ~40 frame names into calls

svg.text: A value moved on a pedal or by MIDI reaches the audio
first: mod-host applies it, then tells the Host. mod-ui
is told afterwards, so a slow UI never delays the sound.
mod-host also talks to Control Chain and the HMI side
without mod-ui: cc_map and pedal values on the CC socket,
plugin LEDs and labels through shared memory (/sys_msgs).
